Incorporating Beige Book evidence into the December 2018 FOMC assessment:

- Beige Book cross-check on current conditions: Multiple Districts reported ongoing growth (including Boston, Philadelphia, Cleveland, St. Louis, Kansas City, Dallas, and San Francisco). Labor markets remained strong with continued job gains, rising wages, and broader nonwage compensation (health benefits, profit-sharing, bonuses, paid vacation). Household spending was supported, with house prices continuing to rise in many markets. Price pressures were mixed across Districts, with falling fuel prices tempering headline inflation—consistent with inflation running near 2%.
- Alignment with the FOMC statement: These District reports reinforce the Committee’s view of strong economic activity, strong labor markets, and inflation near target, supporting the December 25 bp hike and the signal of “some further gradual increases.”
- SLOOS nuance and forward risks: Senior Loan Officer Survey evidence of tighter standards on C&I and construction/land development loans, tighter nonprice terms, and weaker demand in risk-sensitive categories points to more restrictive bank intermediation. This adds a headwind to business fixed investment and growth, amplifying the tightening from rate hikes and balance-sheet runoff.
- Net take: Present conditions are solid and broad-based per the Beige Book, while credit tightening and softer loan demand temper the outlook, especially for capex. Overall tone remains modestly positive but with elevated downside risk to investment and growth.

Adjusting for stronger, broad-based Beige Book signals relative to SLOOS-only guidance, the net sentiment is nudged slightly higher than before.
